lines.say: There's a cruel detail behind this sweet love song
that most people never notice.
This is The Lute Player,
painted by the Italian master Caravaggio.
Most people see a soft-faced boy singing
a madrigal about love.
The open songbook holds love
songs set to verses by Petrarch.
And the picture seems to agree.
His lips part
and his fingers rest gently on the strings.
But look at the cage.
A small songbird sits locked inside it.
According to the story of Cardinal del Monte's household,
a castrato named Pedro Montoya lived there
and sang in the Sistine Chapel.
This rather androgynous model could be him.
Castrati were highly prized at the time.
He isn't a boy singing to a lover.
He's a caged songbird himself.
So is he singing about love,
or about the cage he lives in?
